title: Restriction to a localized site commutes with the sheaf tensor product
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$, and $U$ an object of $\mathcal C$. Let $(\mathcal C/U,\mathcal O_U)$ be the localized ringed site and $\mathcal F\mapsto\mathcal F|_U$ restriction of sheaves of modules to it [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. For sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules $\mathcal F,\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], with sheaf tensor products as in [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], there is an isomorphism of sheaves of $\mathcal O_U$-modules
$$
(\mathcal F\otimes_{\mathcal O}\mathcal G)|_U\cong\mathcal F|_U\otimes_{\mathcal O_U}\mathcal G|_U,
$$
natural in $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$, which for every object $V\to U$ of $\mathcal C/U$ and all $x\in\mathcal F(V)$, $y\in\mathcal G(V)$ sends the image of $x\otimes y$ under the sheafification unit on $\mathcal C$ to the image of $x\otimes y$ under the sheafification unit on $\mathcal C/U$. No finiteness or flatness hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03EL, lemma-tensor-product-pullback, applied to the localization morphism $(j_U,j_U^\sharp)$ of Tag 03DH (section-localize, definition-localize-ringed-site), for which $j_U^*\mathcal F=\mathcal F|_U$.

proof.text: Identify the tensor presheaf of the two restrictions with the restriction of the tensor presheaf by sectionwise identity isomorphisms. Their compatibility with restriction maps and with morphisms in either factor follows by evaluating on pure tensors, which generate each tensor product.

For any module presheaf P, use the module sheafification adjunction on C/U to extend the restricted sheafification unit of P to a linear comparison from the sheafification of the restriction of P to the restriction of the sheafification of P. The adjunction gives its unit equation. Uniqueness of extension, equivalently underlying sheafification hom extensionality, gives naturality in P.

The underlying restricted sheafification unit is locally injective and locally surjective: the original unit is locally bijective, and Over.forget U is cocontinuous, so Mathlib Presheaf.isLocallyInjective_whisker and Presheaf.isLocallySurjective_whisker apply. The slice sheafification unit is also locally bijective. The unit equation and the composition cancellation equivalences for local injectivity and surjectivity imply that the underlying comparison is locally bijective. Mathlib Sheaf.isLocallyBijective_iff_isIso makes it an isomorphism of abelian sheaves, and the module forgetful functor reflects isomorphisms. This directly proves the required special case without invoking the general slice-sheafification compatibility theorem.

Compose the sheafification of the presheaf tensor identification with that comparison, obtaining a module isomorphism c from the localized tensor product to the restriction of the original tensor product. Naturality of the sectionwise identification and of the comparison gives naturality of c in the two factors. Evaluating the sheafification unit naturality equation and the comparison unit equation on x tensor y shows that c carries the localized sheafified pure tensor to the original sheafified pure tensor. Take e to be the inverse of c. Cancel c in the naturality square and apply its inverse to the pure-tensor equation to obtain exactly both clauses of the theorem.
